name: TypeScript
description: Static types for JavaScript: the type system, generics, advanced type-level tools and TypeScript in real projects.

nodes.name: Setup & tsc
nodes.desc: Installing TypeScript, tsconfig.json and compiling with tsc.
nodes.summary: You will be able to install TypeScript, configure a project with tsconfig.json and compile TypeScript to JavaScript with tsc.

nodes.name: Basic types
nodes.desc: Primitive types, arrays, tuples, object types, any and unknown.
nodes.summary: You will be able to annotate values with TypeScript's basic types and choose unknown over any for values of uncertain type.

nodes.name: Type inference
nodes.desc: How TypeScript infers types and when to write annotations yourself.
nodes.summary: You will understand how TypeScript infers types from code and know when an explicit annotation adds value.

nodes.name: Unions & narrowing
nodes.desc: Union and literal types, narrowing with typeof, in and discriminated unions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to model alternatives with union and literal types and narrow them safely with typeof, in and discriminants.

nodes.name: Interfaces & aliases
nodes.desc: Interfaces, type aliases, optional and readonly properties, and extension.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe object shapes with interfaces and type aliases, including optional, readonly and extended properties.

nodes.name: Typing functions
nodes.desc: Parameter and return types, overloads, and typing callbacks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to type function parameters, return values, overloads and callbacks precisely.

nodes.name: Classes in TS
nodes.desc: Access modifiers, abstract classes and implementing interfaces.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write typed classes with access modifiers, abstract members and implemented interfaces.

nodes.name: Modules & .d.ts
nodes.desc: ES modules in TypeScript, declaration files and typing third-party libraries.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use ES modules in TypeScript and write or consume declaration files to type third-party libraries.

nodes.name: Generics
nodes.desc: Generic functions and types, constraints and default type parameters.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write reusable generic functions and types with constraints and default type parameters.

nodes.name: Utility types
nodes.desc: Partial, Pick, Omit, Record, ReturnType and other built-in helpers.
nodes.summary: You will be able to transform existing types with built-in utility types instead of redefining them by hand.

nodes.name: keyof & mapped types
nodes.desc: Index types, keyof, indexed access and mapped types.
nodes.summary: You will be able to derive new types from existing ones with keyof, indexed access and mapped types.

nodes.name: Conditional types
nodes.desc: Conditional types, infer and distributive behaviour over unions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write conditional types, extract types with infer and predict distributive behaviour over unions.

nodes.name: Type guards
nodes.desc: User-defined type guards, assertion functions and exhaustiveness checks with never.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write user-defined type guards and assertion functions and enforce exhaustive handling with never.

nodes.name: Strict mode & config
nodes.desc: Strict compiler flags, project references and migrating JavaScript to TypeScript.
nodes.summary: You will be able to enable strict compiler options, structure large codebases with project references and migrate JavaScript gradually.

nodes.name: Runtime validation
nodes.desc: Validating untrusted data at runtime and deriving static types from schemas.
nodes.summary: You will be able to validate untrusted data at runtime and derive static types from the same schema.
topics: Why static types vanish at runtime

nodes.name: TS with React
nodes.desc: Typing props, state, hooks and events in React components.
nodes.summary: You will be able to type React components, props, state, hooks and event handlers in TypeScript.

nodes.name: TS on the server
nodes.desc: Typed Express handlers, request validation and shared types between client and server.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build typed Express servers with validated requests and share types between client and server.

nodes.name: Typed API client
nodes.desc: Build a fully typed HTTP client library with validated responses and generated types.
nodes.summary: You will build a fully typed HTTP client library with validated responses and types generated from an API schema.
